paper.title_en: Symmetry breaking Poincar{é}--Einstein metrics and non-extendable boundary Killing fields
paper.abstract_en: We construct Poincar{é}-Einstein metrics on $R^2xS^3xS^2xS^2$ which bifurcate from anti-de Sitter black holes whose horizon is the product of a B{ö}hm metric on $S^3xS^2$ with a round $S^2$ , and which break the rotational symmetry of the $S^2$ factor while keeping their conformal infinity. Some Killing fields of the conformal infinity therefore do not extend to the bulk, although $$π$^1(M, $\partial$M ) = 0$. The construction rests on two results of independent interest: the Lichnerowicz eigenvalues of B{ö}hm metrics on invariant transverse traceless tensors are simple (with at most two exceptional values), the lowest one tends to $-$\infty$$ along B{ö}hm's sequence with a gap to the next one tending to infinity; and large anti-de Sitter black holes in dimension nine with an Einstein horizon have no static $L^2$ perturbation of scalar type, which we prove with an explicit positive supersolution of the Kodama-Ishibashi master equation.
